workspace.title: What is a Workspace?
workspace.text1: A Workspace is the place where you and the people you invite can manage shared expenses. Think of it as a "shared account" where all members can see and record movements.
list1: Every user has a default workspace when they sign up
You can create multiple workspaces to separate different contexts
You can invite other people to your workspace
Recorded expenses are visible to all members
Categories and settings are shared within each workspace
list2: Couples or families who want to keep joint track of their household expenses
Roommates who share common expenses (rent, utilities, cleaning)
Freelancers who want to separate expenses by client or project
Owners with multiple properties who need to track expenses separately
workspace.tip: You can switch between your workspaces from the selector in the top bar, next to the logo.

invite.title: How to invite members
invite.text1: You can invite other people to your workspace so they can see and record shared expenses. You only need their email address.
list1: Go to Settings → My Workspace
In the members section, click "Invite"
Enter the person's email address
The person will receive an email with the invitation
Once they accept, they'll be able to see and record expenses in your workspace
invite.tip: Pending invitations appear at the top of the My Workspace tab until the person accepts or rejects them.

movements.title: Movements and expenses
movements.text1: Movements are the heart of the app. Every time you spend money, you can record it to keep detailed track of your finances.
list1: Go to the "Movements" section from the menu
Click the "Movement" button to add a new expense
Fill in the details: amount, currency, bank, payment type, date, description and category
You can also bulk-import movements from the import tab of the same form
Expenses appear in the list sorted by date
You can edit or delete any expense from the table
movements.tip: Use the table filters to search movements by description, type, bank, currency or category.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.text1: Budgets let you set a spending limit per category and currency, and see in real time how much you've spent against that limit.
list1: Go to the "Budgets" section from the menu
Choose the currency you want to view or create budgets for
Create a budget per category: it can be monthly, yearly or recurring (repeats every month)
Each card shows the budgeted amount, the amount spent and a progress bar
The bar changes color as you approach or exceed the limit (green, yellow, red)
You can edit the amount or delete a budget at any time
budgets.tip: If you set up budgets, you'll get alerts on the Balance page when you're close to exceeding your limits.

income.title: Income
income.text1: Income represents your salary or other recurring money inflows. It's configured once and can be set to generate automatically every month.
list1: Go to Settings → My Finances to see the Income section
Add an income entry specifying amount, currency and bank
You can reload (repeat) an existing income entry with one click instead of entering it again manually
Delete an income entry if it no longer applies
income.tip: Turn on "Automatic income" in Settings → Preferences so your configured income entries register themselves as movements every month, without having to enter them manually.

utilities.title: Utilities: recovery time
utilities.text1: The recovery time calculator helps you size up a large expense: it estimates how many months of average savings it would take to recover it.
list1: Go to Utilities from your profile menu (avatar, top right)
Enter the expense amount and currency
Optionally, choose how many months back to use to calculate your average savings (3 by default)
The result shows your average monthly savings and the estimated recovery time
If your average savings for that period were zero or negative, it lets you know the expense isn't recoverable at that rate
utilities.tip: It's a quick reference tool: it doesn't save anything, it just calculates based on your already recorded movements.

settings.title: Settings
settings.text1: From Settings you can configure everything related to your account, your workspace and your finances.
list1: Account: your personal data and user type
Workspace: pending invitations, current workspace and shared categories
My Finances: banks, own currencies and income
Preferences: automations like automatic income
settings.tip: In My Finances you can create your own currencies in addition to the system's global ones. Currencies you create can be freely deleted; global currencies or the one set as your default currency cannot.

services.title: Services and subscriptions
services.text1: Services are recurring expenses that repeat every month. They can be personal (Netflix, Spotify, electricity, gas) or business-related (hosting, domain, software, coworking, insurance).
list1: Go to the "Services" section from the main menu
Fill in the form on the first card to add a new service
Enter the name, monthly amount and whether it's already paid this month
Each service appears as a card you can mark as paid
The summary at the top shows how many services are up to date and how many are pending
services.tip: Recording your services helps you have a clear view of your fixed monthly expenses and never forget to pay one.

balance.title: Balance and reports
balance.text1: The main page shows you a complete summary of your finances for the month. You can see how much you earned, how much you spent and how your expenses are distributed.
list1: The monthly summary shows income, expenses and the net difference
If you have movements in multiple currencies, you can view each one separately
The "Top 5 Categories" shows you where most of your money goes
The pie chart visualizes the distribution by category
The yearly evolution lets you compare month by month, filtering by currency (your selection is saved for next time)
balance.tip: If you set up budgets, alerts will let you know when you're close to exceeding your limits.

admin.title: Admin panel
admin.text1: The admin panel is visible only to users with the Admin role. It lets you manage global settings that affect your entire workspace.
list1: Access it from "Admin" in your profile menu (avatar, top right) — it only appears if you have the administrator role
My Profile: configure your user type (individual or business), which adjusts the labels and text across the whole app
Maintenance: reserved space for future administrative actions
admin.tip: If you don't see "Admin" in your menu, it's because your current role is Family or Guest — ask a workspace administrator to assign you the role if you need it.
